QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_58

question.text: Under SAS-1100, 62% of beneficiaries in the Niwas case are waste-pickers — an extremely vulnerable group. The SIA's evidence-collection plan should therefore:

answer.text: Adapt data-collection: verbal / pictorial survey instruments, informed consent in local language, comfort of community workers present during interview (to reduce intimidation), and trauma-sensitive protocols

explanation.text: The Logic: Vulnerable-group methodology under SAS-1100 requires accessible instruments, in-language consent, comfort-companion (the Niwas case explicitly notes beneficiaries were 'not comfortable without community workers of Swagruha'), and trauma-sensitive protocols. The Trap: Options A, C, B fail accessibility and are unsuitable for waste-pickers. Cross-Exam Context: Vulnerable-group protocols echo XXIV AML KYC adaptation and X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — suitability). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Budget an extra 30-40% fieldwork time for vulnerable-group engagements. Rushed interviews miss the nuance that makes the Report credible.
